---
title: "Logistic and Mixed-Effects Regression"
description: "A two-part medical example about binary outcomes, p-values, and clustered data."
toc: false
---

This lesson follows the same fictional medical study from an ordinary logistic
regression to a mixed-effects logistic regression. The outcome is whether a
patient recovered within 30 days, and patients are grouped within clinics.

::: {.lesson-grid}
::: {.lesson-card}
### [1. Logistic Regression and p-values](1-logistic-regression.Rmd)

Fit a logistic regression, translate log-odds into odds ratios and
probabilities, and interpret p-values without treating them as automatic
decisions about clinical importance.

**Prerequisites:** basic algebra and introductory R.
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [2. Mixed-Effects Logistic Regression](2-mixed-effects-logistic-regression.Rmd)

Account for patients being grouped within clinics, interpret a random
intercept, and compare the result with the ordinary logistic model.

**Prerequisites:** [1. Logistic Regression and p-values](1-logistic-regression.Rmd).
:::
:::
